provenance: Independently written iLab educational statements and proofs with AI assistance. Source item mappings are editorial metadata, not compiler-derived conclusions. See the linked lesson for attribution and assumptions.

laws.label: Primary 1.5 · identity laws
laws.title: Identities do not change a composite
statement: For composable arrows \(f:X\to Y\) and \(g:Y\to Z\),
\[(1_Z\circ g)\circ(f\circ 1_X)=g\circ f.\]
proof: The exact Lean statement inserts an identity before f and an identity after g. Apply the left and right identity laws. Associativity identifies the ordinary composition notation.
laws.limitation: A small consequence of the category laws supplied by the Category instance; it does not construct every category example in the lesson.

inverse.label: Primary 1.11 · inverse uniqueness
inverse.title: A right inverse and a left inverse agree
statement: Let \(f:X\to Y\), \(g,h:Y\to X\), with \(f\circ g=1_Y\) and \(h\circ f=1_X\). Then \(g=h\).
proof: \[g=1_X\circ g=(h\circ f)\circ g=h\circ(f\circ g)=h.\]
The lesson writes the symmetric choice of left/right-inverse names. Both formulations imply uniqueness of a two-sided inverse.
inverse.limitation: Arbitrary independent object and hom universes; the hypotheses are inverse equations, not set-universe axioms.

walking.label: Primary 3.4 / 3.8 / 3.9 · finite equivalence
walking.title: Two isomorphic rooms are equivalent to one room
statement: Let \(\mathbf1\) have one object and \(\mathbb I\) two objects, with one arrow for each ordered pair. The functor \(J:\mathbf1\to\mathbb I\) choosing north has an explicit quasi-inverse.
proof: Collapse both rooms to the single room. The composite in the one-room category is the identity. The other composite is naturally isomorphic to the identity by the unique arrow from north to each room. All required equalities hold because hom types are singletons. Mathlib also checks the triangle condition.
walking.limitation: This concrete adjoint equivalence does not formalize Theorem 3.7 for arbitrary fully faithful, essentially surjective functors.

surjectivity.label: Primary 3.6 / 3.9 · essential versus literal surjectivity
surjectivity.title: Every room is isomorphic to an image
statement: For each room Y, there is an isomorphism from the image of OneRoom.only under includeRoom to Y.
proof: The image is north. The explicitly defined roomIso north Y gives the required isomorphism, for either target object Y.
surjectivity.limitation: The formal essential-surjectivity witness is explicit: Nonempty (includeRoom.obj OneRoom.only ≅ Y). It does not use an unproved general equivalence criterion.

cardinality.label: Primary 3.8 · two-object example
cardinality.title: The two rooms are distinct objects
statement: The finite object type Room has cardinality \(2\).
proof: The instance enumerates north and south and proves completeness by cases. The cardinality proposition is checked by Lean’s ordinary decision procedure.
cardinality.limitation: Cardinality of the object type is not an invariant of categorical equivalence.

nonsurjective.label: Primary 3.6 / 3.9 · literal surjectivity fails
nonsurjective.title: The inclusion misses the south object
statement: The object function of includeRoom is not surjective.
proof: The sole source object maps to north. A putative preimage of south would therefore identify the two distinct constructors; case analysis rules this out.
nonsurjective.limitation: This is failure of literal object surjectivity. A separate theorem supplies essential-surjectivity witnesses.

source.1.1.label: Primary 1.1
source.1.1.title: Set-universe closure: naturals, subsets, powersets, indexed unions
statement: A set-universe U contains ℕ, contains every subset of each of its members, contains the power set of each member, and contains ⋃ᵢ Aᵢ whenever I ∈ U and Aᵢ ∈ U for every i ∈ I.
proof: This is a definition. Existence of such universes is a separate assumption.
source.1.1.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. The library is a set of sets with exact closure conditions, not an actual physical collection. The charter does not prove that a library satisfying it exists. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.2.label: Primary 1.2
source.1.2.title: Russell argument: a universe is not its own member
statement: If U is closed under subsets of its members, then U ∉ U. Under U ∈ U the separation set R = {A ∈ U | A ∉ A} is a member of U; its defining condition at R yields R ∈ R ↔ R ∉ R.
proof: Assume U ∈ U. Subset closure gives R ∈ U. Substitute R into the separation condition and derive a contradiction. Only subset closure is used in this argument.
source.1.2.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Self-listing represents membership, not ordinary book citation. The argument needs a precise separation set and closure hypothesis. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.3.label: Primary 1.3
source.1.3.title: Three nested set-universes and membership assumptions
statement: Assume three set-universes Uₛ ⊆ Uₗ ⊆ Uₕ, together with Uₛ ∈ Uₗ and Uₗ ∈ Uₕ. Inclusion and membership are distinct relations.
proof: The source adopts these conditions as a convention; it does not derive universe existence.
source.1.3.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Lean's type-universe hierarchy is not itself this set-membership statement. A faithful set-theoretic encoding must keep the existence assumptions explicit. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.4.label: Primary 1.4
source.1.4.title: Small, large and huge sets
statement: Relative to the three assumed universes, small sets are members of Uₛ, large sets are members of Uₗ, and huge sets are members of Uₕ.
proof: Terminology defined by membership; the inclusions imply small ⇒ large ⇒ huge.
source.1.4.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. The labels are mathematical universe membership, not numerical bounds or memory limits. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.5.label: Primary 1.5
source.1.5.title: Objects, hom sets, identities, typed composition, unit and associativity laws
statement: A strict category has objects, a hom set C(x,y) for each pair, identities 1ₓ and typed composition. For f:x→y, g:y→z, h:z→t, f∘1ₓ=f, 1ᵧ∘f=f, and (h∘g)∘f=h∘(g∘f). Object and hom sets satisfy the source's large-set bounds.
proof: The laws are part of the category structure, not propositions about every arbitrary graph.
source.1.5.limitation: Checked ordinary type-universe formulation; literal set-coded size bridge not claimed. Arrows need not be functions or journeys. Mathlib categories use type universes; the set-universe existence assumptions remain separate. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.7.label: Primary 1.7
source.1.7.title: Small versus locally small categories
statement: A strict category is locally small if each hom set is small. It is small if it is locally small and its object set is small.
proof: These are definitions. Smallness implies local smallness directly.
source.1.7.limitation: Checked ordinary type-universe formulation; literal set-coded size bridge not claimed. Here small means relative universe size, not finite. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.8.label: Primary 1.8
source.1.8.title: Set, pointed Set, vector spaces, Top; locally small but not small
statement: Sets with functions, pointed sets with point-preserving functions, vector spaces over a fixed small field with linear maps, and topological spaces with continuous maps form locally small strict categories. Under the source's universe convention their object collections are not small.
proof: Identities and composition preserve each specified structure. Hom sets are contained in function sets. The size claim is an additional foundational obligation, separate from the category instances.
source.1.8.limitation: Checked ordinary type-universe formulation; literal set-coded size bridge not claimed. The analogy does not prove closure or the non-smallness claims. These require separate mathematical checks. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.9.label: Primary 1.9
source.1.9.title: Isomorphism, inverse and isomorphic objects
statement: An arrow f:x→y is invertible if there exists g:y→x with g∘f=1ₓ and f∘g=1ᵧ. Objects are isomorphic if such an arrow exists.
proof: Definition; a bundled isomorphism contains the inverse and both equations.
source.1.9.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. An isomorphism need not be equality of objects. One certified round trip is insufficient. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.10.label: Primary 1.10
source.1.10.title: Bijections, pointed bijections, linear bijections and homeomorphisms
statement: Isomorphisms in Set are bijections; in pointed Set they are point-preserving bijections; in Vectₖ they are bijective linear maps; in Top they are homeomorphisms.
proof: Two inverse morphisms give inverse functions. Conversely, the inverse of a bijection preserves the point or linear structure when the forward map does. For topology, inverse continuity is required and is part of a homeomorphism.
source.1.10.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. The story is not a reason to infer inverse continuity. Each category needs its own equivalence between the two descriptions. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.12.label: Primary 1.12
source.1.12.title: Functor object/map data and preservation laws
statement: A functor F:C→D gives an object function and maps C(x,y)→D(Fx,Fy), satisfying F(1ₓ)=1_Fx and F(g∘f)=Fg∘Ff.
proof: These equations define functoriality.
source.1.12.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. A functor need not be injective, surjective or invertible. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.13.label: Primary 1.13
source.1.13.title: Forgetful, added basepoint, free vector space, discrete and indiscrete functors
statement: There are forgetful functors from pointed sets, vector spaces and topological spaces to sets; a functor adjoining a new basepoint; a free-vector-space functor S↦⊕ₛ k; and discrete and indiscrete topology functors from sets to spaces.
proof: Each construction specifies its action on functions and preserves identities and composites. Free linear extension sends each basis vector to the basis vector indexed by its image.
source.1.13.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. These are seven distinct functors. Their adjunction properties are additional results in 3.2. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.16.label: Primary 1.16
source.1.16.title: Size of Cat_s and membership in CAT_s
statement: Catₛ is an object of CATₛ. Catₛ is locally small but not small under the fixed set-universe convention.
proof: The object and functor collections require the larger universe. Local smallness and non-smallness must be assessed separately.
source.1.16.limitation: Checked ordinary type-universe formulation; literal set-coded size bridge not claimed. Type-level universe bounds alone do not establish the source's set-theoretic non-smallness statement. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.18.label: Primary 1.18
source.1.18.title: Contravariant functors as functors from the opposite
statement: A contravariant functor C→D means a functor Cᵒᵖ→D. It sends f:x→y to Ff:Fy→Fx, preserves identities and reverses the order in a composite.
proof: Apply ordinary functor laws to Cᵒᵖ and the opposite composition formula.
source.1.18.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. The direction change is part of the specified domain; it is not arbitrary reversal by an ordinary covariant functor. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.20.label: Primary 1.20
source.1.20.title: Component types and naturality square
statement: A natural transformation α:F⇒G has components αₓ:Fx→Gx such that Gf∘αₓ=αᵧ∘Ff for every f:x→y.
proof: The commuting-square equation is the naturality condition.
source.1.20.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Components need not be isomorphisms, and one checked square does not replace the condition for every arrow. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.22.label: Primary 1.22
source.1.22.title: Componentwise natural isomorphism
statement: A natural transformation is a natural isomorphism when each of its components is an isomorphism.
proof: This defines the componentwise condition; Proposition 1.24 connects it to invertibility in the functor category.
source.1.22.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Having isomorphic image objects does not alone supply a natural family. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.25.label: Primary 1.25
source.1.25.title: Terminal strict category [0]
statement: The terminal strict category [0] has one object and exactly one morphism, its identity.
proof: The unique possible composition satisfies all category laws.
source.1.25.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. A one-object category can have many arrows; [0] specifically has just one. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.1.27.label: Primary 1.27
source.1.27.title: Objects as functors from [0]
statement: An object c of C corresponds to a unique functor [0]→C selecting c.
proof: The object image is prescribed, and preservation of identity forces the only arrow image.
source.1.27.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Uniqueness is for a fixed selected object in a strict presentation. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.2.3.label: Primary 2.3
source.2.3.title: Fully faithful means bijective on each hom set
statement: F:C→D is fully faithful when, for every x,y, its map C(x,y)→D(Fx,Fy) is bijective.
proof: Definition; equivalently each map is both injective and surjective.
source.2.3.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Full faithfulness controls hom sets, not object surjectivity. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.2.6.label: Primary 2.6
source.2.6.title: Detect isomorphisms by all incoming or outgoing hom-set maps
statement: For f:c→d, the following are equivalent: f is invertible; postcomposition C(x,c)→C(x,d) is bijective for every x; precomposition C(d,x)→C(c,x) is bijective for every x.
proof: The authors use full faithfulness of Yoneda and Proposition 1.24 for the incoming-map comparison, then pass to the opposite category for the outgoing-map comparison. They explicitly assign the invertibility equivalence for f and f.op as an exercise; that step is withheld.
source.2.6.limitation: Non-exercise hom-bijection criterion checked; embedded opposite-invertibility exercise withheld. The quantifier is over all objects. A few selected probes need not detect invertibility. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.2.7.label: Primary 2.7
source.2.7.title: Objects are isomorphic iff their representables are naturally isomorphic
statement: Objects x,y of a locally small category are isomorphic if and only if h_x and h_y are naturally isomorphic.
proof: Apply preservation and reflection of object isomorphisms to the fully faithful Yoneda functor, using the componentwise characterization of natural isomorphisms.
source.2.7.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Unstructured bijections between individual hom sets do not suffice; the correspondence must be natural. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.3.1.label: Primary 3.1
source.3.1.title: Left/right adjoints, unit, counit and both triangle identities
statement: An adjunction L:C⇄D:R has unit η:Id_C⇒R∘L and counit ε:L∘R⇒Id_D satisfying ε_Lx∘Lηₓ=1_Lx and Rεᵧ∘η_Ry=1_Ry.
proof: The two triangle identities are part of the definition, alongside naturality of unit and counit.
source.3.1.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Units and counits need not be invertible. An adjunction is generally weaker than an equivalence. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.3.2.label: Primary 3.2
source.3.2.title: Added-basepoint/free-vector and discrete/indiscrete adjunctions
statement: Adjoining a basepoint is left adjoint to forgetting it. Free vector space is left adjoint to its forgetful functor. Discrete topology is left adjoint to the underlying-set functor, which is left adjoint to indiscrete topology.
proof: A pointed map from S with a new basepoint is determined by an arbitrary function on S; a linear map from the free space is determined on basis vectors. Every map from a discrete space is continuous, as is every map into an indiscrete space. These correspondences are natural.
source.3.2.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. There are four distinct adjunctions with specified directions. Forgetting structure is not generally invertible. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.3.4.label: Primary 3.4
source.3.4.title: Equivalence via quasi-inverse and natural isomorphisms
statement: F:C→D is an equivalence if there is G:D→C and natural isomorphisms Id_C≅G∘F and F∘G≅Id_D. The source does not require triangle identities in this definition.
proof: This is the quasi-inverse definition. Its relation to Mathlib's bundled adjoint equivalence requires the upgrade in 3.5.
source.3.4.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Do not silently add triangle identities to the source definition or replace natural isomorphisms by unrelated objectwise ones. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.3.5.label: Primary 3.5
source.3.5.title: Strict isomorphisms and adjoint equivalences imply equivalences
statement: A strict isomorphism of categories is an equivalence. If an adjunction has invertible unit and counit, both adjoint functors are equivalences.
proof: Turn equality of composite functors into identity natural isomorphisms. For an adjunction with invertible unit and counit, the two functors are quasi-inverses; reversing the natural isomorphisms gives the opposite direction.
source.3.5.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. A general adjunction does not have invertible comparisons. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.3.6.label: Primary 3.6
source.3.6.title: Essential surjectivity up to object isomorphism
statement: F:C→D is essentially surjective when for every d∈D there exist c∈C and an isomorphism Fc≅d.
proof: Definition; the witness is an object and an isomorphism, not an equality.
source.3.6.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Essential surjectivity is weaker than surjectivity of the object function. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.3.7.label: Primary 3.7
source.3.7.title: Equivalence iff fully faithful and essentially surjective
statement: A functor is an equivalence if and only if it is fully faithful and essentially surjective.
proof: The source postpones its proof. Independently: an equivalence supplies hom bijections and image representatives. Conversely choose a representative and isomorphism for every target object; full faithfulness uniquely transports arrows between representatives, producing a quasi-inverse and natural isomorphisms. The choice and universe assumptions must remain explicit.
source.3.7.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. The converse uses representative choices. This is an ordinary category theorem; the synthetic foundational setting is not formalized by it. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.3.8.label: Primary 3.8
source.3.8.title: Walking isomorphism: two objects, singleton hom sets
statement: The walking isomorphism I has objects 0 and 1 and exactly one morphism in each hom set. Its nonidentity arrows are mutually inverse.
proof: There is exactly one possible composite with any endpoints, so the category laws and inverse equations hold.
source.3.8.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. Distinct objects remain distinct in the object set even though they are isomorphic. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.3.9.label: Primary 3.9
source.3.9.title: Inclusion of object 0 from [0] into the walking isomorphism is an equivalence
statement: The functor [0]→I selecting 0 is an equivalence.
proof: Its unique hom map is a bijection. Every target object is isomorphic to 0: use the identity for 0 and the specified isomorphism for 1. Alternatively collapse I to [0] and construct the two natural isomorphisms directly.
source.3.9.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. The source proof's printed reference to 0≅0 alone does not account for object 1; the independent explanation explicitly supplies that second case. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.intro.paths.label: Primary intro.paths
source.intro.paths.title: Paths and homotopies fixing endpoints/boundaries
statement: For a topological space, points, paths, endpoint-fixing homotopies and higher boundary-fixing homotopies motivate the fundamental infinity-groupoid. Path concatenation is associative and unital up to homotopy; reversal is an inverse up to homotopy.
proof: The source sketches the construction. The one-dimensional homotopy laws have ordinary topological formalizations; the full infinite construction requires a precise higher model.
source.intro.paths.limitation: Partially checked; higher-foundation obligation remains. A homotopy is a specified continuous deformation. This does not make the parameterized paths literally equal or formalize all higher coherence. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.intro.sip.label: Primary intro.sip
source.intro.sip.title: Indiscernibility, transport and Structure Identity Principle
statement: Equality allows substitution of properties and transport of structures. The intended structure identity principle relates identities of groups to group isomorphisms. Existence of an element of order two is isomorphism-invariant; presentation-specific statements about the identity being the number 0 need not be. The source compares the cyclic group on {0,1} with the multiplicative group {1,−1}.
proof: Equality transport is available in ordinary dependent type theory. Group isomorphisms preserve multiplication, the identity and element order. The structure identity principle requires the intended univalent/homotopical setting.
source.intro.sip.limitation: Partially checked; higher-foundation obligation remains. Group isomorphism is not automatically equality of Lean's bundled groups. A proof of order invariance does not prove the structure identity principle. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.

source.equivalences.motivation.label: Primary equivalences.motivation
source.equivalences.motivation.title: Equality, isomorphism and equivalence-sensitive invariance
statement: Equality, isomorphism and equivalence of strict categories are distinct notions. The one-object category and walking isomorphism are equivalent despite having different numbers of objects.
proof: The explicit functors and natural isomorphisms are given in items 3.8–3.9; the object sets have cardinalities one and two.
source.equivalences.motivation.limitation: Checked definition/hypotheses or proof in the stated Lean formulation. The distinction concerns object presentations and categorical equivalence, not equality of the chosen object sets. Each referenced signature specifies the precise checked formulation.
